surplus_policies.institution: University of Texas at San Antonio (UTSA)
surplus_policies.summary: Equipment may be sold to non-UTSA organisations or individuals only by auction (internet or public) run by Surplus Property; UTSA keeps the proceeds. Items are first offered to UTSA departments and then to the UTSA community. University-sourced merchandise is treated as its own category: it is the only property the guideline lets be transferred or sold outside its scope. Guideline 1401 says only the Surplus Property Department may dispose of or sell surplus.
surplus_policies.caveat: The brief says 1402 restricts third-party resale and NIL items. That wording was NOT confirmed: the page could not be fetched (utsa.edu blocked), and search snippets did not show any NIL or third-party-resale clause. Confirm the full text before citing it.

surplus_policies.summary: Disposal and resale of athletic apparel and equipment must be approved by the associate athletics director for Compliance and the executive senior associate AD for Business Operations; staff must check with Compliance before donating items.
Student-athletes may not sell school-issued equipment, apparel or awards while athletically eligible.
Same rule: student-athletes may not sell school-issued gear while eligible.
A student-athlete may keep athletics apparel (not equipment) at the end of their collegiate participation, and may buy used equipment on the same terms as any other buyer.
Disposition by highest and best use; 85% of proceeds go back to the unit; surplus must be disposed of or recycled (no donations); this includes surplus from the sports venues.

surplus_policies.policy: Procedure 720.2 Acquisition and Disposal of Surplus and Salvage University Property
surplus_policies.summary: Property worth $10,000 or more (individually or as a lot) must be offered to other UC locations before any public sale; departments face restrictions on buying back their own surplus.

surplus_policies.policy: Directive - Public Sale of Surplus Property
surplus_policies.summary: Public auctions through Public Surplus and GovDeals, plus fixed-price sales.
Governs public sale of OSU surplus property.

surplus_policies.policy: Disposal of Surplus University Property Policy
surplus_policies.summary: Baylor's institutional disposal policy (content not read).
Outside requests for donated auction items were reviewed for compliance with SMC, WCC and NCAA rules, and Athletics reserved the right to refuse.
The 50% back-to-school student discount excludes athletic apparel.
Capital and controlled assets are sold only by public auction through the contracted auctioneer; employees and students cannot buy directly.
Items sold as-is with no warranty, refunds or returns; all sales in person.

surplus_policies.summary: Student-athletes are generally barred from selling team-issued apparel and equipment such as jerseys and cleats; NIL changes did not obviously lift this. This affects the provenance of player-sourced items, not institutional surplus sales.
